harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Published node1’s approved release tree as the persistent, read-only rsync module `releases`. Node2 retrieved it with modes and symlinks intact. Uploads and access outside the module are denied. Both nodes retained CentOS Stream 10, kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64, and rsync 3.4.1. Sequential restart testing succeeded on both nodes.
actions_performed: Configured and enabled rsyncd on node1, bound to its managed IP.
Restricted daemon access to node2 and confined the module to the releases directory with chroot.
Configured SELinux for read-only rsync export and kept anonymous writes disabled.
Retrieved the complete release tree on node2 using archive semantics.
Verified file hashes, modes, ownership, and the `current -> v1` symlink.
Confirmed uploads, sibling-module access, and traversal outside the release tree fail.
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Publish a persistent read-only rsync module named releases on node1
evidence.summary: Shows the active/enabled daemon, managed-IP listener, module path, chroot and read-only configuration, node2-only firewall rule, and SELinux write denial.

evidence.requirement: Node2 retrieves the full tree with modes and symlinks intact
evidence.summary: Shows actual transfers plus the preserved 0644 and 0755 modes, `current -> v1` symlink, and matching SHA-256 hashes before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Writes and access outside the release tree are denied
evidence.summary: Both initial and post-restart tests reject upload, the unexported `private` module, and `../private` traversal.
Baseline and final manifests/hashes match on both nodes; the protected private file remains mode 0600 with its original hash.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel using compatible software
evidence.summary: Baseline and final evidence show CentOS Stream 10, kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64, and rsync 3.4.1 unchanged on both nodes.
Captures healthy baseline boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered daemon/listener/data, and successful remote module access.
Captures healthy baseline boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, fresh post-restart retrieval, and intact recovered data.
